domain: Religious Studies / Textual Hermeneutics / Ethical Philosophy
topic_summary: Analysis of the Bhagavad Gita as a contested kernel where orthodox literal readings mandate caste-based duty (svadharma) and justify physical violence in righteous war versus allegorical readings (exemplified by Gandhi) that reinterpret the battlefield as internal spiritual struggle. The interpretive divergence determines whether the text authorizes caste hierarchy and violence or repudiates both.

key_entities: Bhagavad Gita (Sanskrit scripture; Chapter 18 verses on svadharma and caste duty)
Arjuna (warrior facing moral crisis over killing kin)
Orthodox Brahminical tradition (interprets text as caste-duty mandate)
key_tensions: Literal vs allegorical hermeneutic authority (who legitimately interprets the kernel)
Caste hierarchy preservation vs egalitarian spiritual universalism

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The Bhagavad Gita's discourse at Kurukshetra stabilizes as shared textual substrate across interpretive traditions
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Legitimacy derives from claimed fidelity to the text's 'true meaning' — contested between scholastic lineages (śāstraic authority) and reformist moral intuition

readings.commitment: Text mandates caste-based duty and legitimates righteous violence in dharmic war
readings.authority_grounding: Brahminical scholastic tradition; Shankaracharya commentarial lineage; scriptural literalism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Caste hierarchy enters beneficiary set (as divinely ordained social order); kshatriya warrior class justified in violence when duty-bound; Brahmins retain interpretive monopoly; victims are lower castes locked in hierarchy and those killed in 'righteous' war

readings.commitment: Kurukshetra battlefield is metaphor for internal struggle; violence is spiritual not physical
readings.authority_grounding: Reformist moral intuition; appeal to broader Hindu ethical principles (ahimsa); rejection of caste as divinely fixed
readings.expected_structural_delta: Caste hierarchy exits constraint set (no divine mandate); physical violence repudiated; interpretive authority shifts from Brahminical scholars to individual moral conscience; ahimsa elevated as supreme principle; victims are those subjected to structural violence of caste and literal war

readings.commitment: Text teaches path-independent devotion (bhakti) accessible to all regardless of caste; dharma is surrender to divine will not social role
readings.authority_grounding: Bhakti movement; Vaishnava traditions; emphasis on Krishna's Chapter 9 promise of universal salvation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Caste as spiritual barrier dissolved; duty redefined as devotional surrender not social role; violence neither mandated nor central to text's message; egalitarian access to salvation; beneficiary is universal devotee class; traditional Brahminical gatekeeping authority undermined

axiom_contradictions.basis: Orthodox reading holds caste hierarchy as divinely fixed ontological reality requiring enforcement; Gandhian reading holds caste as human construct requiring abolition. No framework can simultaneously affirm caste as divine law and repudiate it as illegitimate social construction.

Orthodox reading grounds spiritual authority in birth-caste and ritual knowledge monopoly; universalist reading makes devotion path-independent of caste. No framework can hold both Brahminical gatekeeping and universal devotional access as simultaneously valid principles.

axes.human_readable: Orthodox Literal Reading (Caste Duty as Divine Mandate)
axes.structural_delta: Text interpreted as literal mandate for caste-based duty and justified violence in righteous war
axes.primary_observable: Commentarial tradition emphasis on svadharma verses; caste endogamy maintenance; scriptural authority cited for varna system
axes.selection_reason: Core reading establishing maximum extractiveness (caste hierarchy plus violence justification); highest beneficiary/victim asymmetry

axes.structural_delta: Battlefield reinterpreted as metaphor for internal moral struggle; violence and caste repudiated
axes.primary_observable: Gandhian writings on Gita; nonviolence movement rhetoric; rejection of caste as divinely sanctioned
axes.selection_reason: Structurally opposed reading collapsing both caste and violence constraints; demonstrates kernel contestation

axes.structural_delta: Devotional surrender replaces caste-duty as primary teaching; spiritual access universalized
axes.primary_observable: Bhakti movement texts; Vaishnava commentaries emphasizing Chapter 9; cross-caste temple access debates
axes.selection_reason: Third structurally distinct reading dissolving caste gatekeeping via alternative authority principle (devotion over birth)

omegas.description: Neo-Vedanta readings (Vivekananda, Aurobindo) synthesize literal and allegorical elements, claiming both caste critique and dharmic duty coexist in text. Does this represent fourth reading or collapse under coherence test?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — syncretic traditions not decomposed

omegas.description: Dalit Buddhist and Ambedkarite readings reject Gita entirely as Brahminical oppression tool. Is rejection itself a reading or exit from kernel entirely? Affects victim-set boundaries.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — anti-caste readings that refuse engagement

omegas.description: British colonial translations (e.g., Charles Wilkins 1785) shaped 'orthodoxy' perception in anglophone discourse. Is received 'orthodox' reading itself a colonial construction layered over pre-colonial diversity?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — anglophone academic framing as unexamined interpretive layer

omegas.description: Does orthodox reading justify all violence or only dharmic war violence? Constraint scope ambiguity affects epsilon measurement. Text's own ambiguity (Krishna's vishvarupa terror) may be load-bearing for interpretive contest.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) concern — violence justification scope unclear

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: Orthodox reading's violence justification scope unclear — text may authorize only specific kshatriya war-duty not general violence, but 20th century Hindu nationalism expanded scope.
